apply_texts: Again no square. The warmth is familiar, and still the teeth will not agree with themselves.
Again the empty turn. It is only metal. The oval does not deepen, and the mind keeps its count.
No square takes the key. Warmth climbs the pinch, and the teeth disagree before you finish.
The half-turn finds nothing to wind. The pinch is poor work. The unease, after a moment, thins.
The last turn sticks. The bow cools all at once, the oval fixed, as if the pinch had finished its work.
The same half-turn, heard twice and then not at all. The oval under the thumb is newly cruel.
You give the key a half-turn. No clock answers. Under the thumb the oval is, already, deeper.
You turn it once more. The teeth seem fewer, then not. You set the winder down before the count settles.
inspect_texts: A half-turn has worried the bow. The oval is deeper, though no works answered the key.
The bow is nearly round, yet the pinch seems to wait. Nothing has been wound, and the waiting is too precise.
The bow is not round. The pinch looks shut like a mouth, and the silver is warmer than silver.
The crookedness is steady. You can name the miss, yet the name will not stay upon the teeth.
The metal has cooled where the thumb worked. The oval holds its new depth, and the teeth hesitate.
The silver bow is nearly round. One edge pinches inward, as if a thumb had not yet left it.
The winder sits crooked. Each look shortens one tooth and lengthens another, and the count fails.
You have turned it. The oval deepens, and the teeth will not number the same way twice.
native.name: Crooked Winder
